title: Top Things to Do in Karlovac, Croatia 2027
metaDescription: Top things to do in Karlovac: Zvijezda star fortress, Dubovac Castle, Aquatika aquarium, Korana promenade, city museum and Beer Days, with hours and € prices.
content:
## Zvijezda: The Star-Shaped Old Town

Zvijezda is the historic core of Karlovac and the reason most visitors come. Construction began on 13 July 1579 on the orders of Archduke Charles II of Habsburg, after whom the town is named. The plan was a six-pointed Renaissance fortress on flat ground at the meeting point of rivers, built to block Ottoman advances toward Zagreb and Ljubljana.

The fortress is large: roughly 400 m by 600 m, with a moat and outer wall extending about 150 m further. The ramparts are now green parks, and the star outline is clearest from a map or aerial view rather than from street level. On foot, the grid of streets around Trg bana Jelačića, the central square, is compact. A slow walk of the whole core takes 1 to 1.5 hours and costs nothing.

Start at Trg bana Jelačića, then follow the park belts that trace the old moat. The Zrinski promenade and Zrinski Park sit on the green ring and work well for a break between sights. The Church of the Holy Trinity on the main square is a landmark of the centre.

### Karlovac City Museum

The City Museum covers the building of the fortress, life inside it, and the town's history up to the present. Allow about one hour. The display is chronological, and the attic shows details of the bridge works from the 16th century to the bridge's removal in 1881. Many labels are in Croatian, but the museum offers guided visits in several languages, so ask at the desk.

Hours are Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 8:00 to 16:00, Wednesday 8:00 to 19:00, Saturday 10:00 to 16:00 and Sunday 10:00 to 12:00. It is closed on Monday. Hours can change seasonally, so confirm before visiting on a Sunday.

## Dubovac Castle

Dubovac Castle is the oldest monument in the Karlovac area and predates the star fortress by centuries. The settlement is first mentioned in 1339. It stands on a hill about 185 m above sea level, above the Kupa. Medieval owners included the Frankopan and Zrinski families. When Zvijezda was built on the plain, the castle lost its military role. Its current look comes from a major restoration in the mid-20th century.

The tower is the main reason to go. A museum inside the tower tells the castle's story, and the top gives a view over the whole city, the course of the Kupa and the surrounding hills. On a clear day the view reaches toward Slovenia, about 12 km away in a straight line. The castle also has a restaurant and hosts concerts and events.

**Opening hours:**
- 1 June to 30 September: Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 to 20:00
- 1 October to 31 May: Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 to 18:00
- Closed Mondays and public holidays. Last entry is 30 minutes before closing.

**Getting there:** From the centre it is a walk of about 10 minutes uphill. Plan 1 to 1.5 hours for the castle and tower. Go in the last two hours before closing in summer for softer light over the rooftops and river.

The address is Zagrad-Gaj 5. The castle is run by the same organisation as the City Museum, so opening rules are shared.

## Aquatika Freshwater Aquarium

Aquatika is the first and only freshwater aquarium in Croatia. It is built around the four rivers of Karlovac: the Kupa, Korana, Mrežnica and Dobra. The pools follow the course of a typical karst river such as the Korana, from spring to lowland. About 100 fish species are shown, including around 40 endemic species.

**Address:** Ulica Branka Čavlovića Čavleka 1a, near the city stadium.

**Hours:** 1 April to 31 October, daily 9:00 to 19:00. 1 November to 31 March, daily 9:00 to 17:00. Closed on Easter, Christmas and New Year's Day.

**Ticket prices:**
- Adults: €12
- Children aged 3 to 14: €7
- Teens 15 to 18, students, pensioners: €8
- Family (2 adults + up to 3 children): €24
- Guided visit: €25 per group (book ahead)
- Audio headset: about €2.50

**Honest verdict:** Aquatika is small. Most visitors finish in 30 to 45 minutes. It is excellent for children and a good wet-weather option, but it is not worth a special trip alone, and adults travelling without children can skip it if time is short. Buy the family ticket if there are four or five of you, since it saves a lot against individual prices. There is a cafe outside.

## Rivers: Korana, Kupa and Foginovo

Karlovac is known as the city of four rivers, and the water is the main reason locals spend time outdoors.

### Korana promenade

The Korana runs along the edge of the old town. The walk beside it is flat and shaded, with cafes and terraces. It is the best place for an evening coffee or a cold beer. The promenade also hosts the main stages of Beer Days.

### Foginovo river beach

Foginovo is the city's main swimming spot on the Korana. In summer, locals swim, sunbathe and picnic here. Water quality and bans can change after incidents, so check the city's current swimming notices before packing a towel. A fire in late August 2026 led to a temporary swimming ban downstream of Mala Švarča, including Foginovo, so confirm that the ban has been lifted.

### Kupa walks

The Kupa flows below Dubovac. The riverside paths are easy and level, and fit well with a visit to the castle. A walk from the old town to the riverbank takes about 15 minutes.

## Karlovac Beer Days (Dani Piva)

Karlovačko beer has been brewed in the city since 1854, when the brewery was founded by Baron Nikola Vranyczany-Dobrinović. The annual Beer Days festival is the longest-running beer event in Croatia. The 2025 edition was the 38th and ran from 29 August to 2 September. It runs for five days in late summer, with concerts, food stalls and craft beer stands.

**Costs in 2025:** A 0.5 l Karlovačko on tap was €2.50. Drinks were served in recyclable cups, and ten used cups could be exchanged for a free beer. A special festival train ran from Zagreb for about €1.50 return on the busiest days.

**Brewery access:** The brewery is a working Heineken plant, not a regular museum. Guided tours have mainly been offered on the festival's Open Doors Day, hourly from 10:00 to 17:00 in 2025. Outside the festival, check availability with the tourist board before planning around a visit.

Don't believe the idea that the brewery tour is a year-round must-do. The brewery itself is the least reliable item on a Karlovac list, and the festival, the river terraces and the Zvijezda walk are all easier and better value.

## Practical Tips for First-Time Visitors

- **Distance:** Karlovac is about 55 km from Zagreb. Trains and buses take around 1 hour.
- **Best day:** Visit Tuesday to Saturday. The City Museum and Dubovac are closed on Mondays.
- **Best order:** Walk Zvijezda in the morning, visit the City Museum, have lunch near the Korana, then go up to Dubovac for the late afternoon.
- **Time needed:** One full day covers all the main sights. A half day covers Zvijezda, Dubovac and a river walk.
- **Money:** Karlovac is cheaper than the coast. Lunch at a local restaurant is typically in the €10 to €15 range, and a coffee about €2.
- **Footwear:** The castle hill and cobbled sections reward comfortable shoes.
- **Shoulder season:** April to June and September are mild and quieter. Winter is calm, and Aquatika then closes at 17:00.

## Suggested One-Day Plan

1. **9:00** Walk the Zvijezda park ring and Trg bana Jelačića.
2. **10:30** City Museum (about 1 hour).
3. **12:00** Lunch near the Korana.
4. **13:30** Aquatika (45 minutes), especially with children.
5. **15:30** Climb to Dubovac Castle, visit the tower museum and view.
6. **18:00** Evening walk by the Korana or Kupa.

## Where Karlovac Fits Among Croatian Cities

Karlovac is not a coastal resort. It is a calm inland town whose main strengths are a well-preserved Renaissance plan, a medieval castle, river scenery and a beer tradition. It suits travellers who want a relaxed, low-cost stop between Zagreb and the coast, or a short city break of one to two days.

faq.question: What are the top things to do in Karlovac?
faq.answer: The main sights are the Zvijezda star-shaped old town, Dubovac Castle with its tower view, Aquatika freshwater aquarium, the City Museum, and the Korana and Kupa riverbanks. In late summer, Beer Days adds a major festival.

faq.question: How much time do you need in Karlovac?
faq.answer: One day covers all major sights. A half day is enough for Zvijezda, Dubovac Castle and a riverside walk, while Aquatika adds about 45 minutes.

faq.question: How much does Aquatika aquarium cost?
faq.answer: Adult tickets cost €12 and children aged 3 to 14 pay €7. Students and pensioners pay €8, and a family ticket for 2 adults and up to 3 children costs €24. It is open daily 9:00 to 19:00 from April to October, and 9:00 to 17:00 from November to March.

faq.question: When is Dubovac Castle open?
faq.answer: From 1 June to 30 September it is open Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 to 20:00. From 1 October to 31 May it is open Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 to 18:00. It is closed on Mondays and public holidays, and last entry is 30 minutes before closing.

faq.question: When is the Karlovac Beer Days festival?
faq.answer: Beer Days takes place over five days in late August and early September. The 2025 edition ran from 29 August to 2 September. A 0.5 l beer on tap cost €2.50 that year, so check the official site for current dates.

faq.question: Is Karlovac worth visiting?
faq.answer: Yes, for one day or a stop on the way to the coast. It has a well-preserved Renaissance fortress layout, a medieval castle, river walks and lower prices than coastal towns. It is not a high-energy destination, and the aquarium is small.

faq.question: How far is Karlovac from Zagreb and how do you get there?
faq.answer: Karlovac is about 55 km from Zagreb. Trains and buses take around 1 hour, and driving by motorway takes a similar time. From the centre, Dubovac Castle is a 10-minute uphill walk.

quickAnswer: The top things to do in Karlovac are walking the 1579 Zvijezda star-shaped old town, climbing Dubovac Castle tower, visiting Aquatika, Croatia's only freshwater aquarium (adults €12), and exploring the city museum. Add a stroll along the Korana and Kupa rivers, and a visit during Beer Days in late summer.
